To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is a statistically significant difference between the Turkish and American students in algebra-based physics courses in their attitudes and approaches toward physics problem solving, and that the Turkish students are on average more novice-like in their attitudes and approach to physics problem solving

there are statistically significant differences between Turkish high school and university physics students on some items of the Turkish version AAPS survey, that Turkish university students in general display more expert-like attitudes than vocational high school physics students, and that there are differences between the responses of Turkish and American university physics students on the Turkish AAPS survey.

there is evidence that the Turkish version of AAPS survey can be used to measure attitudes and approaches of Turkish high school and university physics students, and that the responses of Turkish high school students are different from those of Turkish university students and American university students.

the attitudes and approaches of high school and university level students in Turkey to physics problem solving and the differences between these groups.

the Turkish students are more expert-like than their vocational high school peers, but they are less expert-like than their university peers in the US.
the Turkish students are not as expert-like as their US counterparts, but they are more expert-like than their vocational high school peers in Turkey.

the Turkish version of AAPS survey can be used to assess Turkish students' attitudes and approaches to solving physics problems.
